summary: The paper proves the rank-zero p-converse for CM elliptic curves over their imaginary quadratic CM field, and over Q by descent, for every prime including 2. It obtains the required rational CM Kato main conjecture from the elliptic-unit equivariant main conjecture, then combines the converse with Smith's and BKLOS's Selmer statistics. The extraction separates reusable existing owners from two new Part II proof branches and preserves all-prime, rational-coefficient, Tate-twist and density conventions.

conventions: K is imaginary quadratic with chosen complex embedding; Qbar embeds in C and C_p, and chosen compatible local embeddings define localization maps. These are ambient choices, not new mathematical structures.
For modular statements, k≥2 is the cohomological range of Kato (8.3); k is even for central half-weight statements. A prime p is arbitrary unless a separate input explicitly restricts it.
V(f) is Kato's cohomological representation. Its determinant and Tate dual differ from the common covariant modular convention; f* denotes coefficient conjugation.
H^q at Z[1/p] uses the generic-point j_* convention of Kato (8.2), not j_! and not unrestricted cohomology after arbitrarily enlarging S.
All main-conjecture equalities proved here are over the completed Iwasawa ring with p inverted, not over an integral ring and not an unrestricted formal power series ring Q_p[[T]].
Relative densities, lower limiting proportions and orderings are spelled out; no finite Selmer rank is silently identified with p∞-corank.

items.name: The classical p-power Selmer group
items.statement: For an elliptic curve E over a number field F and a rational prime p, Sel_{p∞}(E/F) is the kernel of H¹(F,E[p∞]) → ∏_v H¹(F_v,E)[p∞], equivalently the direct limit of finite-level Kummer Selmer groups with their transition maps. Local conditions are the images of E(F_v)⊗Q_p/Z_p.
items.locator: §1.0.1, p.1; applied over K in Theorem 1.1
items.note: Finite-level elliptic theory is upstream; the infinite-level/local-condition comparison is imported, not recreated. The pinned concrete 2-descent group is not this p∞ object.

items.name: The Tate–Shafarevich group
items.statement: For an elliptic curve E over a number field F, Sha(E/F)=ker(H¹(F,E) → ∏_v H¹(F_v,E)); Sha(E/F)[p∞] is its p-primary subgroup.

items.name: Kummer–Selmer exact sequence
items.statement: For E/F as above and every prime p, the Kummer maps give 0 → E(F)⊗_Z Q_p/Z_p → Sel_{p∞}(E/F) → Sha(E/F)[p∞] → 0.

items.name: Selmer corank
items.statement: For the cofinitely generated discrete Z_p-module Sel_{p∞}(E/F), its Z_p-corank is dim_{Q_p}(Sel_{p∞}(E/F)^∨⊗_{Z_p}Q_p), with the continuous Pontryagin dual and contragredient action.

items.name: Analytic rank of an elliptic curve
items.statement: For the actual analytically continued Hasse–Weil L-function of E, ord_{s=1} L(s,E/F) is its order of vanishing at 1; order zero means L(1,E/F)≠0. For the CM curves over K here continuation is supplied through the Hecke-character factorization, not assumed for arbitrary number-field curves.
items.note: BSD.0 supplies the analytic rank over Q; over K the order of vanishing of the CM newform L-functions is planned by ModularForms Layer 7. The CM/K factorization itself is the separate missing item cm-elliptic-factorization. For ord_{s=k/2} of a newform see newform-l-function. WeierstrassCurve.LFunction and WeierstrassCurve.LSeries are the formal Euler product and Dirichlet series of E over any number field; Mathlib proves no convergence or continuation for them, and ord_{s=1} must be taken of the continuation, never of WeierstrassCurve.LSeries. The planned claim covers E/Q and its base change to a quadratic K (BSD.0; ModularForms Layer 7 for newforms); for CM E/K in general, including curves that do not descend, the continuation and order come from cm-elliptic-factorization.

items.name: Analytic rank at most one determines Mordell–Weil rank
items.statement: For E/Q, if ord_{s=1}L(s,E/Q)=r with r=0 or r=1, then rank_Z E(Q)=r.

items.name: Analytic rank at most one implies finite Sha
items.statement: For E/Q, if ord_{s=1}L(s,E/Q)≤1, then Sha(E/Q) is finite.

items.name: The rank-r p-converse proposition
items.statement: For E/Q, prime p and integer r≥0, the rank-r p-converse denotes the implication corank_{Z_p}Sel_{p∞}(E/Q)=r ⇒ ord_{s=1}L(s,E/Q)=r. This names a proposition; the paper does not prove it for arbitrary E, p and r.
items.note: Only the rank-zero CM instance is proved unconditionally here.

items.name: Complex multiplication by an order of the base CM field
items.statement: An elliptic curve E/K in the paper has K imaginary quadratic and its geometric endomorphism ring an order O⊂K, with the CM action over K; the order need not be maximal. Curves E/Q are considered via their CM base change.
items.note: The geometric CM predicate and endomorphism carrier stay upstream; the CM roadmap supplies order/ideal-action comparisons.

items.name: All-prime CM rank-zero converse over K
items.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic, E/K an elliptic curve with complex multiplication by an order of K, and p any rational prime. If corank_{Z_p}Sel_{p∞}(E/K)=0, then ord_{s=1}L(s,E/K)=0.
items.note: No restriction on ordinary reduction, good reduction, p splitting, p>2, or p∤#O_K^×.

items.name: All-prime CM rank-zero converse over Q
items.statement: Let E/Q be a CM elliptic curve and p any rational prime. If corank_{Z_p}Sel_{p∞}(E/Q)=0, then ord_{s=1}L(s,E/Q)=0.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1, final sentence, p.1; final paragraph of its proof, p.6

items.name: Quadratic twist indexed by a squareclass
items.statement: For E/F over a number field and t∈F×/(F×)², E^(t) is the twist of E by the quadratic character associated with F(√t)/F, including the trivial squareclass. For a short model y²=x³+Ax+B, the model t y²=x³+Ax+B is equivalent to y²=x³+t²Ax+t³B.
items.note: Near match read: tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwistOf and quadraticTwist. The pinned trace/norm carrier exists, but a squareclass-indexed family with this model dictionary, including the trivial class, is not supplied merely by its name.

items.name: Congruent-number twist family
items.statement: Fix E/Q:y²=x³−x. For nonzero integer n, E^(n) is given by n y²=x³−x; the counting family restricts to positive squarefree n.
items.locator: Abstract, p.1 (model ny²=x³−x); §1.0.2 (twist E^(n), n∈Z∖{0}) and Theorem 1.2 (E: y²=x³−x; positive square-free n), p.2
items.note: An instance of the planned quadratic twist (item twist) for the curve y²=x³−x; nothing beyond the twist carrier and its model dictionary is needed.

items.name: Relative density in the even-parity congruent-number family
items.statement: Let S(X)={n∈Z:0<n≤X, n squarefree, n mod 8∈{1,2,3}}. A subset A has density one in this family when # (A∩S(X))/#S(X) tends to 1 as X tends to infinity.
items.note: Retain positive squarefree ordering; do not substitute fundamental-discriminant ordering without a comparison.

items.name: Root-number criterion for congruent-number twists
items.statement: For positive squarefree n, the global root number of E^(n):n y²=x³−x is +1 exactly when n≡1,2,3 (mod 8); it is −1 in the remaining positive squarefree residue classes.
items.locator: Footnote 2 to Theorem 1.2, p.2; cited Birch–Stephens [2]
items.note: Specialize the root-number/functional-equation infrastructure of BSD.0; source-scoped calculation, not an assertion of parity for algebraic rank. The classification is for positive n: n=−1≡7 (mod 8) has root number +1, since E^(−1)≅E.

items.name: Even-parity Goldfeld for the congruent-number curve
items.statement: For a relative-density-one subset of positive squarefree n≡1,2,3 (mod 8), ord_{s=1}L(s,E^(n)/Q)=0 for E:y²=x³−x. Consequently the proportion with analytic rank zero among all positive squarefree n tends to 1/2.
items.note: The conclusion does not include analytic rank one on a density-one subset of the odd-parity classes. This is BT's squarefree formulation; the fundamental-discriminant formulation is goldfeld-fundamental.

items.name: Even parity Goldfeld conjecture for E/Q
items.statement: For E/Q and a fundamental discriminant d, let E^(d) be the quadratic twist by the character of Q(√d). The even parity Goldfeld conjecture for E asserts that #{d fundamental, |d|≤X, ord_{s=1}L(s,E^(d)/Q)=0} / #{d fundamental, |d|≤X} → 1/2 as X→∞, with both signs of d.
items.locator: §1.0.2, p.2 (footnote 1's odd-parity companion is not included)
items.note: Use tauceti:TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsFundamentalDiscriminant for the index set, the item twist for E^(d), the item analytic-rank, and ArithmeticStatistics ST.0 for the |d| ordering.

items.name: Even parity Goldfeld for y²=x³−x
items.statement: For E: y²=x³−x the even parity Goldfeld conjecture (goldfeld-conjecture) holds.
items.locator: Theorem 1.2 first clause, p.2; abstract, p.1
items.note: Derive it from goldfeld and congruent-root-number, with E^(d)≅E^(n) for d∈{n,4n}, E^(−1)≅E via x↦−x, and a counting lemma: each class |n| mod 8 ∈ {1,2,3,5,6,7} of squarefree integers has density 1/π²; fundamental discriminants with n≡1 mod 4 are counted to |n|≤X and those with n≡2,3 mod 4 to |n|≤X/4, so for each sign the root-number +1 and −1 classes have equal weight. Import the counting from ST.0 and squarefree-half.

items.name: Height ordering on number-field squareclasses
items.statement: For a number field F and t∈F×/(F×)², put H(t)=∏_{finite primes 𝔭 with v_𝔭(t) odd} N𝔭. Count squareclasses with H(t)<X, unweighted. For F=Q this is absolute value of the squarefree representative; for K this is the ordering used in Proposition 1.3 via BKLOS §2.
items.locator: Proposition 1.3, p.2; Theorem 3.5, p.7; BKLOS §2, p.2
items.note: The exact height is supplied by the cited input, not stated in BT's shorthand '50%'. Establish bounded-height finiteness via units modulo squares and finite ideal classes; do not use a height of arbitrary representatives. The height was checked against BKLOS §2: H(s)=∏_{v_𝔭(s) odd}N𝔭, each squareclass counted once with H(s)<X.

items.name: At least half of CM twists over K have analytic rank zero
items.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic, E/K have CM by an order in K, and assume 3 is not inert in K (split or ramified is allowed). Among t∈K×/(K×)² ordered by H(t), the lower limiting proportion with ord_{s=1}L(s,E^(t)/K)=0 is at least 1/2.
items.note: Use a lower-density assertion, not existence of an exact 50% limit or a density-one theorem.

items.name: Cyclotomic Z_p-extension in the introductory formulation
items.statement: For p prime, Q_∞/Q is the cyclotomic Z_p-extension and Λ_cyc=Z_p[[Gal(Q_∞/Q)]]. In §1.0.3 this is the torsion-free quotient tower, whereas §2 uses the full Q(μ_{p∞}) tower.

items.name: Strict Selmer module of the cyclotomic tower
items.statement: For T=T_p(E), take the Selmer condition with zero local condition at p and the source's unramified conditions away from p over Q_∞; the compact Pontryagin-dual Iwasawa module is X_st(E/Q_∞). Use the action involution fixed by the Selmer owner when comparing characteristic ideals.
items.note: BT calls X_st the strict Selmer group; the characteristic-ideal formulation uses its compact module convention. No ordinary/Greenberg replacement is permitted.

items.name: Cyclotomic deformation of the elliptic Beilinson–Kato element
items.statement: For E/Q, T=T_p(E), let z_E∈H¹(Q,T)⊗Q_p be its Beilinson–Kato element and bold z_E the Iwasawa class in H¹(Z[1/p],T⊗Λ_cyc)⊗Q_p specializing to it, with the inverse Galois action on the induced completed coefficient module.

items.name: Rational Kato main-conjecture proposition
items.statement: With the preceding elliptic/cyclotomic conventions, the rational main-conjecture proposition asserts X_st is Λ_cyc-torsion and char_{Λ_cyc[1/p]}(H¹_Iw(T)[1/p]/Λ_cyc[1/p]·bold z_E)=char_{Λ_cyc[1/p]}(X_st[1/p]). This is a proposition, not a theorem for every elliptic curve.
items.note: MIMC L0 states Kato's conjecture only as char H²_Iw = char(H¹_Iw/Λ z_Kato). The X_st form (i)–(ii) and its Poitou–Tate comparison with H²(Z[1/p], T⊗Λ) over Λ[1/p] are not stated by any stage. BT use the X_st form only in §1.0.3, whose notation 'is not followed in the rest of the article'. Theorem 2.6 (cm-kato-main) and Remark 3.2 (conditional-converse) use the H² form, so no route is needed.

items.name: Compatible roots of unity and Tate-twist convention
items.statement: For a fixed prime p choose primitive p^n-th roots ζ_{p^n} in Qbar with ζ_{p^{n+1}}^p=ζ_{p^n}. This fixes the trivialization used in the Iwasawa twist isomorphism; changing the compatible generator changes coordinates, not the Tate module.

items.name: Continuous p-adic cyclotomic character
items.statement: For p prime the character ε:G_Q→Z_p× is characterized by g(ζ)=ζ^{ε(g) mod p^n} on every p^n-th root of unity. It is a continuous group homomorphism for the Krull topology.
items.note: Statements read in Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean at 082e2d3; take L an algebraic closure and restrict ring automorphisms to Gal(L/Q). The fallback trivial character for fields without enough roots is irrelevant here.

items.name: Localization of a module at a prime
items.statement: For a commutative ring R, prime ideal q and R-module M, M_q=(R\q)^{-1}M, an R_q-module.
items.note: Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LocalizedModule/Basic.lean, lines 49–52 and 85–90: the general localization accepts a multiplicative submonoid; use q.primeCompl. This does not claim a characteristic-ideal API exists.

items.name: Ray class field in a fixed algebraic closure
items.statement: For an imaginary quadratic K embedded in C and nonzero ideal a⊂O_K, K(a) is the ray class field of modulus a inside K^ab, using global Artin reciprocity; no real-place modulus is present.

items.name: Two-variable ray-class tower
items.statement: Fix imaginary quadratic K, p prime and nonzero ideal f. Set K(p∞f)=∪_n K(p^n f) and G_{p∞f}=Gal(K(p∞f)/K), with its profinite topology and finite-level restriction maps.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0 builds the ray-class inverse limit with its reciprocity interpretation, and ClassFieldTheory Layer 13 the ray class fields. The CM extension imports the tower rather than rebuilding it.

items.name: Structure of the CM ray-class Galois group
items.statement: With K,p,f as in the preceding item, G_{p∞f} is topologically isomorphic to Z_p²×Δ_f for a finite abelian group Δ_f. No prime-to-p order is assumed for Δ_f.
items.note: Planned by the dimension formula of AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0, which keeps all torsion factors: for imaginary quadratic K the unit group is finite and there is no Leopoldt defect, so the free rank is 2.

items.name: Semilocal coefficient ring for the CM tower
items.statement: For the preceding G, R=Z_p[[G]] is the completed group ring, a three-dimensional commutative semilocal ring; retain finite torsion factors and rationalize before using character projectors when p divides #Δ_f.
items.note: The Z_p carrier Z_p[[G]] (completed group algebra, commutative for abelian G, with its compact modules) comes from ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 9; its one-variable power-series coordinate does not apply to Z_p²×Δ_f. PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1/L4 supply the coefficient change to a finite O, the rationalization R[1/p] and multivariable module theory. G's arithmetic structure is the planned item ray-group-structure (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0).

items.name: Norm-compatible p-unit module
items.statement: For the tower K(p∞f), h¹=lim_{K'} (O_{K'}[1/p]×⊗_Z Z_p), where K' runs through finite subextensions and transitions are norms; use its natural continuous R-action.
items.note: The S-unit groups are finitely generated, so completion/tensor comparison must be proved in this regime, not asserted for K'×.

items.name: Norm-compatible p-primary class module
items.statement: For the same tower, h²=lim_{K'} Cl(K')[p∞], with norm transition maps and its natural continuous R-action.

items.name: Finite generation of CM tower units
items.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic, p any prime and f a nonzero ideal, with R,h¹,h² as above. h¹ is finitely generated over R.
items.note: Generic finite generation/control interfaces do not themselves prove these arithmetic tower-specific assertions.

items.name: Finite generation of CM tower class groups
items.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic, p any prime and f a nonzero ideal, with R,h¹,h² as above. h² is finitely generated over R.
items.note: Generic finite generation/control interfaces do not themselves prove these arithmetic tower-specific assertions.

items.name: Torsion-freeness of CM tower units
items.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic, p any prime and f a nonzero ideal, with R,h¹,h² as above. h¹ is torsion-free over R: no nonzero element is killed by a non-zero-divisor of R.
items.note: Generic finite generation/control interfaces do not themselves prove these arithmetic tower-specific assertions.

items.name: Generic rank of CM tower units
items.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic, p any prime and f a nonzero ideal, with R,h¹,h² as above. For each height-zero prime q of R, h¹_q has dimension one over the field R_q.
items.note: Generic finite generation/control interfaces do not themselves prove these arithmetic tower-specific assertions.

items.name: Torsion of the CM tower class module
items.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic, p any prime and f a nonzero ideal, with R,h¹,h² as above. h² is a torsion R-module.
items.note: Generic finite generation/control interfaces do not themselves prove these arithmetic tower-specific assertions.

items.name: Elliptic-unit submodule
items.statement: For K,p,f as above, let z⊂h¹ be the R-submodule generated by the norm-compatible elliptic units ({}_a z_{p^n f})_n for integral ideals a prime to 6pf. At sufficiently large n the modulus admits the canonical CM pair of Kato §15.5; norm compatibility supplies the remaining components. The auxiliary smoothing factors are part of the construction.
items.note: Do not replace elliptic units by cyclotomic units or arbitrary norm-compatible S-units.

items.name: Elliptic units have torsion quotient
items.statement: In the same CM ray tower and for every prime p, h¹/z is a torsion R-module.

items.name: Rational characteristic ideal
items.statement: Let Λ=O[[Z_p^d×Δ]] with O the ring of integers of a finite extension of Q_p, d∈{1,2} and Δ finite abelian; the instances are R=Z_p[[G_{p∞f}]] (d=2, Δ=Δ_f), Λ_cyc=Z_p[[Gal(Q_∞/Q)]] (d=1, Δ trivial) and O_λ[[G_∞]] (d=1, Δ≅Z/(p−1), or Z/2 when p=2). For a Λ-module M set M_Q=M⊗_Z Q=M[1/p]. For a finitely generated torsion Λ[1/p]-module N, ξ(N) is the ideal determined by the lengths of N at the height-one primes q with p∉q, taken componentwise after coefficient extension.
items.locator: §1.0.3, item (ii), p.2; §2.1.1, last paragraph, p.3; Theorem 2.6, p.5
items.note: No information at primes containing p survives. Integral p-torsion idempotents cannot be obtained by dividing by #Δ_f before this rationalization.

items.name: CM main conjecture at horizontal height-one primes
items.statement: For imaginary quadratic K, prime p, nonzero f, and each height-one prime q⊂R=Z_p[[G_{p∞f}]] with p∉q, length_{R_q}((h¹/z)_q)=length_{R_q}((H²_{pf})_q)=length_{R_q}(h²_q)+Σ_{𝔩|f,𝔩∤p}length_{R_q}(Z_p[[G_{p∞f}/D_𝔩]]_q). In particular length(h²_q)=length((h¹/z)_q) when q lies on a component ramified at every such 𝔩.
items.note: JLK §7.2 treats regular primes. Their singular-prime/μ hypothesis in §7.3 is not required for this assertion and cannot be dropped from an integral extension. Corrected by review: JLK §7.2 works with H² over O_K[1/pf]; equating it with h² needs the Euler terms of h2-euler-comparison. JLK's argument holds for every p, including p=2, 3 and non-split p (their Theorem 5.2 is "for all primes p with no exceptions"; the p=2 inputs are Itakura's preprint and Rubin's Euler-system Theorem 2.3.3).

items.name: Rational equivariant CM main conjecture
items.statement: For imaginary quadratic K, any prime p and nonzero ideal f, ξ((h¹/z)_Q)=ξ(h²_Q)·∏_{𝔩|f, 𝔩∤p}ξ(Z_p[[G_{p∞f}/D_𝔩]]_Q) as ideals of Z_p[[G_{p∞f}]][1/p], D_𝔩 the decomposition group of 𝔩; equivalently ξ((h¹/z)_Q)=ξ((H²_{pf})_Q) with H²_{pf}=lim_{K'}H²(O_{K'}[1/pf],Z_p(1)). The printed form ξ(h²_Q)=ξ((h¹/z)_Q) holds when every prime factor of f lies above p, and after localizing at any height-one prime lying on a component ramified at every 𝔩|f with 𝔩∤p.
items.note: Corrected by review. As printed, Theorem 2.1 omits the Euler factors at the primes of f prime to p: z uses only the modulus-p^n f elliptic units (Kato §15.5), whose projections carry ∏(1−χ(𝔩)Frob_𝔩^{−1}) (Johnson-Leung–Kings Lemma 7.7), while h² is the class-group limit, which Kato (15.6.2) identifies with H² over O[1/p], not over O[1/pf] as in JLK. On the trivial-character component the factor is a non-unit even after inverting p. The same imprecision is in Kato's quotation of Rubin (Thm 15.2(2)); Rubin's elliptic units include all moduli g|f. The paper's later results are unaffected: Theorem 2.6 uses the equality only on ψ-components, f the conductor of ψ, where every such 𝔩 is ramified and the factors are units.

items.name: Kummer comparison for CM tower units
items.statement: For the above ray tower, h¹ is naturally isomorphic to lim_{K'}H¹(O_{K'}[1/p],Z_p(1)), compatibly with norm/corestriction and the R-action.

items.name: Class groups and H² agree in codimension one
items.statement: For the above ray tower there is a map h²→lim_{K'}H²(O_{K'}[1/p],Z_p(1)) whose kernel and cokernel are finitely generated Z_p-modules; consequently it is an isomorphism at every height-one prime of R. The proof retains the p-place class and Brauer correction terms before passing to codimension one.
items.note: The tower-specific pseudo-null error calculation is extra to the generic Selmer/class-group comparison.

items.name: Euler-factor comparison of the two H² modules
items.statement: For K imaginary quadratic, p prime and nonzero f, write H^i_S=lim_{K'}H^i(O_{K'}[S^{-1}],Z_p(1)) over finite K⊂K'⊂K(p∞f). Then H¹_p=H¹_{pf}, and restriction gives an exact sequence 0→H²_p→H²_{pf}→⊕_{𝔩|f, 𝔩∤p}Z_p[[G_{p∞f}/D_𝔩]]→0, where D_𝔩 is the decomposition group of 𝔩, of Z_p-rank one. Each Z_p[[G_{p∞f}/D_𝔩]] is torsion but not pseudo-null, and its localization vanishes at every prime of R[1/p] lying on a component where the inertia group of 𝔩 acts nontrivially.
items.locator: Implicit in Theorem 2.1 and footnote 3, p.4; Johnson-Leung–Kings §4.2 (purity as in Lemma 4.3) and Lemma 7.7
items.note: Added by review. JLK's main conjecture concerns H²_{pf}; BT's h² is the class-group limit, which Kato (15.6.2) identifies with H²_p at height one. These Euler terms are why Theorem 2.1 needs correcting (item equivariant-main); they vanish on the ψ-components used in Theorem 2.6.

items.name: Normalized elliptic newform
items.statement: For N≥1 and integral weight k≥2, f∈S_k(Γ₁(N)) is a nonzero cusp form with nebentypus, a good-Hecke eigenform in the new subspace, normalized by a₁(f)=1. Being an eigenform at all bad indices is a theorem, not an extra coordinate in this definition.
items.note: Read TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/Newform.lean, lines 75–107. This imports only the actual bundled newform definition, not the absent bad-index or coefficient-field theorems.

items.name: Hecke field and coefficient completion
items.statement: For such a newform put F=Q(a_n(f):n≥1), a number field; for a place λ|p use its completion F_λ and ring of integers O_λ.
items.note: The newform carrier exists; coefficient-field arithmetic is a separate unbuilt target in the reviewed ModularForms Layer 8 audit.

items.name: Kato's cohomological modular representation
items.statement: For f of weight k≥2 and λ|p as above, V_{F_λ}(f) is the two-dimensional continuous G_Q-representation the quotient of the étale cohomology of the open modular curve Y₁(N) with Sym^{k−2} coefficients by the Hecke ideal generated by the T(n)−a_n(f), in Kato's cohomological convention (6.3, 8.3). For k=2 and f attached to E/Q, V(f)≅V_pE^*≅V_pE(−1). A stable O_λ-lattice T is chosen. Its determinant is ε_cyc^{1−k} ε_f^{-1}, not the dual convention ε_f ε_cyc^{k−1}.
items.note: The existing roadmap's realization must be compared explicitly with Kato's dual/Tate normalization. Weight one is not included in the cohomological construction used here.

items.name: The full cyclotomic Galois tower
items.statement: For n≥0, G_n=Gal(Q(ζ_{p^n})/Q) and G_∞=lim_n G_n=Gal(Q(μ_{p∞})/Q), with restriction maps. This is not just the cyclotomic Z_p quotient.

items.name: Cyclotomic identification and its inverse elements
items.statement: The cyclotomic character induces a topological group isomorphism κ:G_∞≃Z_p×; for c∈Z_p× define σ_c=κ^{-1}(c).
items.note: The baseline character alone is not this infinite-tower topological equivalence.

items.name: Finite factor at odd primes and at two
items.statement: Topologically Z_p×≃Z_p×Δ, where Δ≃Z/(p−1) for p odd and Δ≃Z/2 for p=2; at p=2 the procyclic factor is 1+4Z_2 and the finite factor is {±1}.

items.name: Full cyclotomic Iwasawa coefficient ring
items.statement: For the place λ|p, Λ=O_λ[[G_∞]] is a two-dimensional complete semilocal ring. The rational coefficient ring for Theorems 2.3–2.6 is Λ_Q=Λ⊗_Z Q=Λ[1/p].

items.name: Kato's étale Iwasawa cohomology
items.statement: For T⊂V_{F_λ}(f) stable and each integer q, H^q_Iw(T)=lim_n H^q(Z[ζ_{p^n},1/p],T), with corestriction transitions and Λ-action; H^q_Iw(V)=H^q_Iw(T)⊗_Z Q. The finite-level term means H^q(Spec R,j_*T) as in Kato (8.2), where j is the generic-point inclusion, with lattice cohomology obtained from finite quotients.
items.note: Use j_* (not j_!) and retain bad-prime conditions. An unrestricted G_{Q,S}-cohomology group is not a drop-in replacement. The j_* convention is identified with unramified local conditions in jstar-selmer-comparison.

items.name: Kato’s j_* cohomology as a Selmer complex
items.statement: For a number field F and a p-power-torsion G_F-module M unramified outside a finite set, RΓ_et(O_F[1/p], j_*M) is quasi-isomorphic to the Selmer complex with unramified conditions RΓ(G_{k_v}, M^{I_v}) at every finite v∤p and no condition at v|p, by the localization triangle and the stalk (j_*M)_v̄ = M^{I_v}. The identification is compatible with corestriction and lattice change and passes to lattices T by the limit over T/p^n. Hence Kato's H^q_Iw(T) is the Iwasawa cohomology (SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3) of that Selmer complex; it has the same H¹_Iw as unrestricted G_{Q,S}-cohomology, while H²_Iw differs by ⊕_{ℓ|N} H²_Iw(Q_ℓ,T).
items.locator: Kato 8.2 and 12.2, as used throughout BT §2
items.note: A source addition to SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2, with the Iwasawa limit in L3.

items.name: Rational Iwasawa cohomology is lattice independent
items.statement: For any two G_Q-stable O_λ-lattices in V_{F_λ}(f), the finite-index comparison maps induce canonical isomorphisms between H^q_Iw(T)⊗Q; these comparisons commute with restriction, corestriction and specialization.
items.note: Kato 12.2 states only independence of the lattice T; the compatibilities with restriction, corestriction and specialization are routine additions not stated there.

items.name: Kato's rational H² torsion theorem
items.statement: For any normalized elliptic newform f of weight k≥2, prime p, and λ|p, H²_Iw(V_{F_λ}(f)) is a torsion Λ_Q-module.
items.note: A modular arithmetic theorem, not a generic consequence of defining Iwasawa cohomology. L4's nonvanishing/Euler-system bounds supply this source-scoped input; no residual irreducibility or ordinary hypothesis is inserted into the rational statement. The planned KatoEulerSystems:L4 status covers non-CM f only: L4 plans the §13 Euler-system bound (Kato Thm 13.4), whose hypothesis (v) fails for CM f (Kato p.226). The non-CM case is used only by conditional-converse (Remark 3.2); the CM case is cm-h2-torsion.

items.name: Kato's rational H¹ freeness theorem
items.statement: For the same f,p,λ, H¹_Iw(V_{F_λ}(f)) is free of rank one over Λ_Q.
items.note: Generic L3 finite generation and Kato L4 divisibility do not explicitly plan this freeness statement. Route as an exact additional source target in Kato L4, not a new cohomology owner. For CM f this follows from cm-h2-torsion by Kato 13.8 and 13.9–13.13 (Kato 15.16); (15.16.1) itself uses 12.4(2). Kato states 15.16 only for K ⊄ Q(μ_{p∞}); for K ⊂ Q(μ_{p∞}) (K=Q(i), p=2) the same deduction applies, since 13.9–13.13 use only 12.4 and 13.5–13.6.

items.name: Beilinson–Kato zeta map
items.statement: For every normalized elliptic newform f of weight k≥2 and λ|p, Kato constructs a nonzero F_λ-linear map V_{F_λ}(f)→H¹_Iw(V_{F_λ}(f)), γ↦z_γ(f).
items.note: For CM f this follows from cm-h2-torsion by Kato 13.8 and 13.9–13.13 (Kato 15.16); (15.16.1) itself uses 12.4(2). Kato states 15.16 only for K ⊄ Q(μ_{p∞}); for K ⊂ Q(μ_{p∞}) (K=Q(i), p=2) the same deduction applies, since 13.9–13.13 use only 12.4 and 13.5–13.6.

items.name: Module of Beilinson–Kato elements
items.statement: Z(f) is the Λ_Q-submodule of H¹_Iw(V_{F_λ}(f)) generated by z_γ(f) for all γ∈V_{F_λ}(f). It is not specified by choosing one arbitrary zero or wrong-sign vector.

items.name: The Beilinson–Kato quotient is torsion
items.statement: For f,p,λ as in Theorem 2.4, H¹_Iw(V_{F_λ}(f))/Z(f) is a torsion Λ_Q-module.
items.note: For CM f this follows from cm-h2-torsion by Kato 13.8 and 13.9–13.13 (Kato 15.16); (15.16.1) itself uses 12.4(2). Kato states 15.16 only for K ⊄ Q(μ_{p∞}); for K ⊂ Q(μ_{p∞}) (K=Q(i), p=2) the same deduction applies, since 13.9–13.13 use only 12.4 and 13.5–13.6.

items.name: Critical-value characterization of the Kato map
items.statement: Let f be a weight-k≥2 newform, 1≤r≤k−1, n≥0, χ a character of G_n, and γ in its rational Betti realization V_F(f). Twist z_γ by k−r using the chosen roots, specialize at Q(ζ_{p^n}), localize at p and apply exp*. Kato's χ-weighted period comparison with sign (−1)^{k−r−1}χ(−1) sends the result to (2πi)^{k−r−1} L^{ {p} }(f*,χ,r) γ^{±}. Here f* has complex-conjugate Fourier coefficients and L^{ {p} } omits the p-factor; the untwisted full L-value used in §3 requires the associated local-factor comparison. These interpolation conditions uniquely characterize the F_λ-linear zeta map.
items.locator: Remark 2.5, p.5; Kato Theorem 12.5(1), printed p.221
items.note: Use Kato's period-map equality, not equality of a raw cohomology class and a complex number. For γ∈V_{F_λ}, extend the equality F_λ-linearly. The exact same normalization is required in the central-value corollary. The f* in the formula was checked visually on Kato printed p.221; passing to f at a real critical integer uses coefficient conjugation.

items.name: Infinity type of a Hecke character
items.statement: For an imaginary quadratic K with fixed complex embedding and integers m,n, a Hecke character ψ:C_K→C× has infinity type (m,n) when its restriction to C× is z↦z^m·bar(z)^n.
items.note: The carrier and infinity types belong to GlobalNumberFields; CM.4 constructs the particular characters, not a second Hecke-character definition.

items.name: L-function of a newform
items.statement: For a normalized newform f∈S_k(Γ₁(N)), k≥2, L(s,f) is the entire function equal to Σ_{n≥1}a_n(f)n^{-s} for Re s>k/2+1 (arithmetic normalisation, centre k/2); ord_{s=k/2}L(s,f) is its order of vanishing at k/2.
items.note: Apply these to the toCuspForm of tauceti:HeckeRing.GL2.Newform (width 1). The degree-two Euler product and the named analytic rank at k/2 stay planned by tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-7-l-functions (AUDIT-16).

items.name: CM newform in the arithmetic normalization
items.statement: A CM newform f of weight k≥2 is the normalized cuspidal theta/automorphic-induction form attached to an algebraic Hecke character ψ of an imaginary quadratic K of infinity type (1−k,0).
items.locator: §2.2.5, p.5; Kato 15.10, p.260; Kato's own definition, Remark 12.8, p.223, is by L(f,s)=L(ψ,s)
items.note: The definition is the image of automorphic induction. R17.5 and R16.6 plan only the direction from ψ to f; its agreement with Kato's hypothesis and with the ModularForms Layer 9 CM predicate is cm-characterization.

items.name: L-function of an algebraic Hecke character
items.statement: For K imaginary quadratic with fixed embedding ι and an algebraic Hecke character ψ of infinity type (1−k,0) and conductor f, L(s,ψ)=∏_{𝔭∤f}(1−ψ(𝔭)N𝔭^{-s})^{-1}=Σ_{(𝔞,f)=1}ψ(𝔞)N𝔞^{-s} for Re s>(k+1)/2, values taken through ι (arithmetic normalisation), together with its analytic continuation to C.
items.locator: §2.2.5, p.5, and the proof of Theorem 1.1, p.6
items.note: AL.1 owns the continuation; AN.4 keeps the ideal-series comparison under RS-07. The carrier is GlobalNumberFields Layers 9–10, as in hecke-infinity-type.

items.name: CM newform–Hecke L-function comparison
items.statement: For f and ψ in the preceding CM correspondence, L(s,f)=L(s,ψ) in arithmetic normalization, initially by the Euler factors and then by analytic continuation, with conductor and bad factors matched.
items.note: The special-case elliptic regulator theorem ER.5 is not a supplier for arbitrary CM newforms or nonmaximal orders. L(s,f) is newform-l-function. L(s,ψ) is hecke-l-function.

items.name: CM case of Kato Theorem 12.4
items.statement: For a normalized CM newform f of weight k≥2 attached to ψ of conductor f, any prime p and λ|p, H²_Iw(V_{F_λ}(f)) is a torsion Λ_Q-module; hence (Kato 13.8, as invoked in 15.15) H¹_Iw(V_{F_λ}(f)) is Λ_Q-free of rank one.
items.locator: Theorem 2.3, p.4, CM case; Kato 15.15 p.265, 15.14 p.264
items.note: Kato does not prove 12.4 for CM f with the §13 Euler-system bound (Thm 13.4): its hypothesis (v) fails in the CM case (Kato p.226). Proof outline (Kato 15.15): extend coefficients to L ⊇ F containing the values of ψ and use V_L(f) ≅ Ind ψ. At each height-0 prime of O_λ[[G_∞]] let q be its inverse image in O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]]; q has height one and p ∉ q. H¹_{p∞f}(V(ψ))_q is free of rank one and the image of z_{p∞f}⊗V(ψ)(−1) is nonzero by 13.5 and (15.12.2), so it generates. Rubin's inequality (Kato 15.2(1), condition (a)), or regular-prime-equality after twisting, gives H²_{p∞f}(V(ψ))_q = 0, and (15.13.1), or its §15.14 form when K⊂Q(μ_{p∞}), gives H²(V~(ψ))_p = 0. Use only (15.12.2), not (15.16.1), since (15.16.1) itself uses 12.4(2). K=Q(i), p=2 (needed for Theorem 1.2) is the §15.14 case. Uses cm-elliptic-reciprocity for (15.12.2).

items.name: Kato’s λ-adic realization of a CM Hecke character
items.statement: For ψ of type (−r,0), r≥1, with L=K(ψ(K̂^×)): V_L(ψ)=H¹(E(C),Q)^{⊗r}⊗_K L and V_{Lλ}(ψ)=H¹_ét(E⊗Q̄,Q_p)^{⊗r}⊗_{K⊗Q_p}L_λ, for (E,α) the canonical CM pair over K(f); the Gal(Q̄/K)-action descended by η_ψ=ψ(a)^{-1}(η_a^*)^{⊗r}, on which (a,K(p∞f)/K) acts by ψ(a)^{-1}; S(ψ)⊂coLie(E)^{⊗r}⊗_K L and per_ψ:S(ψ)→V_C(ψ); the isomorphism (15.8.1) S(ψ)⊗_L L_λ≅D^j_dR(K⊗Q_p,V_{Lλ}(ψ)) for 1≤j≤r; and independence of f.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.6, p.5; Kato 15.8, pp.256–257
items.note: CM.4 covers only the r=1 rank-one components of Tate modules. The items cm-descent, equality-descent, cm-zeta-bridge and cm-kato-main use V_L(ψ) and V_{Lλ}(ψ) as defined here.

items.name: Kato’s CM comparison map (15.12.1)
items.statement: The O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]]-map H¹_{p∞f}(V_{Lλ}(ψ))→H¹(V_{Lλ}(f)), obtained through H¹(V(f))=H¹(V~(ψ)) (via (15.11.2) of cm-galois-induction) and K⊗Q(ζ_{p∞})→K(p∞f).
items.note: cm-zeta-bridge compares units and Kato classes through this map.

items.name: Kato’s explicit reciprocity for elliptic units
items.statement: Kato Prop. 15.9 as printed, for every r≥1, every prime p, every nonzero f contained in the conductor of ψ and every finite K′⊂K(p^∞f), followed by its consequence (15.12.2) with γ′ taken under (15.11.3).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.6, p.5 (via (15.16.1)); Kato Prop. 15.9, p.258, its proof pp.258–260, and (15.12.2), p.263
items.note: The proof has two parts: (a) the height-one case of [KK3, Thm 4.3.1], applied to the p-divisible groups G(v,𝔭) of the canonical CM curve over K(𝔤); (b) the Eisenstein-series period evaluation (15.9.1). It is not supplied by KatoEulerSystems L3 (modular curves, h=2) or by ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity (Shimura reciprocity). PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21/elliptic-reciprocity is its r=1 specialization in BKO's convention and imports it.

items.name: Elliptic units specialize to Beilinson–Kato elements
items.statement: For a CM newform f induced from ψ, enlarge coefficients to a field L containing the values of ψ and the Hecke field. Under Kato's CM cohomological comparison (15.12.1) and his period-compatible comparison isomorphism (15.11.3) (the Galois identification V~_{Lλ}(ψ) ≅ V_{Lλ}(f) that (15.12.1) uses is (15.11.2), Kato's standing identification for §15, p.262; (15.11.3) is used only to define γ' from γ, never as an identification, Kato p.263), z_{p∞f}⊗γ⊗(ζ_{p^n})_n^{−1} maps to z_{γ'}(f), where γ∈V_L(ψ) and γ' is its image in V_L(f). Here z_{p∞f} is the auxiliary-independent fraction-field elliptic-unit element of (15.6); its localized span is z_q at height one.
items.note: This is a named comparison of actual units and actual Kato classes, not an arbitrary identification of rank-one modules. Integrality is not asserted. For CM f this follows from cm-h2-torsion by Kato 13.8 and 13.9–13.13 (Kato 15.16); (15.16.1) itself uses 12.4(2). Kato states 15.16 only for K ⊄ Q(μ_{p∞}); for K ⊂ Q(μ_{p∞}) (K=Q(i), p=2) the same deduction applies, since 13.9–13.13 use only 12.4 and 13.5–13.6. Uses cm-realization for V_{Lλ}(ψ), cm-galois-induction for V(f)≅Ind V(ψ), and cm-comparison-map for (15.12.1). Uses cm-elliptic-reciprocity for (15.12.2).

items.name: Iwasawa cohomology of the ray tower with general coefficients
items.statement: For K imaginary quadratic, p prime, f nonzero and T a finitely generated Z_p-module (or O_λ-lattice) with continuous Gal(K̄/K)-action unramified almost everywhere, H^q_{p∞f}(T) = lim_{K'} H^q(O_{K'}[1/p], T) over finite K ⊂ K' ⊂ K(p∞f), with Kato's j_* étale convention (8.2) at finite levels and corestriction transitions. It is a finitely generated O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]]-module and vanishes for q ≠ 1, 2.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.6, p.5; Kato 15.6, p.253
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3 plans H^i_Iw only for Z_p^d-extensions, and G_{p∞f} ≅ Z_p² × Δ_f; it could instead be planned there if that layer is widened to Z_p^d × finite towers. cm-descent and equality-descent use it.

items.name: Rational ray-tower to cyclotomic cohomology descent
items.statement: In Kato §15, suppose the CM field K is not contained in Q(μ_{p∞}); let L contain the character and Hecke values, λ|p, and let f be the conductor of ψ, and let q be the inverse image of a prime r of O_λ[[G_∞]] under the surjection O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]]→O_λ[[G_∞]] induced by restriction (ψ enters only through the coefficient module T). If 2 and #Δ_f are invertible in the residue field at r, both localized rings are regular and the map's kernel is principal, say (a). For a stable lattice T in V_{L_λ}(ψ), H²_{p∞f}(T)_q/a≅H²_cyc(Ind_K^Q T)_r and 0→H¹_{p∞f}(T)_q/a→H¹_cyc(Ind_K^Q T)_r→H²_{p∞f}(T)_q[a]→0 is exact.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.6 and footnote 4, p.5; Kato Lemma 15.13
items.note: After inverting p the finite integer factors become units. The H²[a] term is retained until proved to vanish; ordinary specialization is not automatic. Uses cm-realization for V_{Lλ}(ψ), cm-galois-induction for V(f)≅Ind V(ψ), and cm-comparison-map for (15.12.1). H^q_{p∞f}(T) is ray-coefficient-iwasawa-cohomology.

items.name: Descent when the CM field lies in the cyclotomic tower
items.statement: When K⊂Q(μ_{p∞}), put G'_∞=Gal(Q(μ_{p∞})/K). The descent statement uses G'_∞ and Kato's H^q(T) on that tower; the induced cohomology over Q is H^q(T)⊗_{O_λ[[G'_∞]]}O_λ[[G_∞]]. With these replacements Lemma 15.13 supplies the comparison used in the CM main-conjecture argument.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.6, p.5; Kato §15.14 and last paragraph of Proposition 15.17
items.note: Important at p=2 for K=Q(i): do not apply the disjoint-tower case to the congruent-number application.

items.name: Twisted equivariant main conjecture on a lattice
items.statement: Let ψ have conductor f, T ⊂ V_{L_λ}(ψ) a stable lattice and χ: G_{p∞f} → O_λ^× the character of T(−1). (a) H^q_{p∞f}(T) ≅ (H^q_{p∞f}(Z_p(1)) ⊗_{Z_p} O_λ) ⊗ T(−1), semilinear for Tw_χ: g ↦ χ(g)^{±1}g with the sign fixed by Kato's σ^{-1} convention in Lemma 15.13; it carries z ⊗ O_λ to the span of z_{p∞f} ⊗ T(−1) at height one (Kato (15.6.4)). (b) H¹_{p∞f}(T)_q is torsion-free of rank one. (c) For every height-one prime q' ∌ p contained in q, the inverse image of a prime r ∌ p of O_λ[[G_∞]] (O_λ[[G'_∞]] when K ⊂ Q(μ_{p∞})): length(H²_{p∞f}(T)_{q'}) = length((H¹_{p∞f}(T)/A·(z_{p∞f}⊗T(−1)))_{q'}).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.6, p.5; Kato 15.15 and Prop. 15.17 proof, p.265
items.note: (b) follows from (a) with units-kummer, units-torsionfree and units-rank-one. (c): twist by (a), apply class-cohomology, units-kummer and equivariant-main over O_λ, then kill the Euler terms of h2-euler-comparison: g−1 ∈ q for g ∈ I_𝔩 and χ|_{I_𝔩} = ψ|_{I_𝔩} ≠ 1, so O_λ[[G/D_𝔩]]_{Tw(q')} = 0. This carries equivariant-main (Z_p(1) coefficients) to the hypothesis of equality-descent.

items.name: From the equivariant equality to Kato's equality at one-variable primes
items.statement: In the setting of Kato Lemma 15.13 (K⊄Q(μ_{p∞}), f the conductor of ψ, r a prime of O_λ[[G_∞]] with p∉r, q its inverse image, A=O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]]_q a regular local ring whose kernel to O_λ[[G_∞]]_r is generated by a prime element a), and in its §15.14 variant, put M₁=H²_{p∞f}(T)_q and M₂=H¹_{p∞f}(T)_q/A·(z_{p∞f}⊗T(−1)). If length(M₁)_{q'}=length(M₂)_{q'} at every height-one prime q' of A, then length(H²(T~)_r)=length(H¹(T~)_r/Z(ψ,T)_r). Proof: apply Kato's Lemma 14.15 to M₁ and M₂ and use (15.13.1)–(15.13.2); the Ker(a|H²) terms cancel, and Ker(a|M₂)=0 because A is a UFD, H¹_{p∞f}(T)_q is torsion-free of rank one and z generates it at aA (Kato 15.15).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.6, p.5; not in Kato, whose §15 proves only the inequality (Prop. 15.17, p.265)
items.note: Added by review. BT write that Kato §15 shows the CM case of Conjecture 12.10 follows from the equivariant main conjecture. Kato proves the inequality from Rubin's inequality, and says he does not use Rubin's equality (p.251). This lemma is the missing equality step. The integrality of z_{p∞f}⊗T(−1) at q, implicit in Kato's own proof, must be checked in the blueprint. Uses cm-realization for V_{Lλ}(ψ), cm-galois-induction for V(f)≅Ind V(ψ), and cm-comparison-map for (15.12.1). Its hypothesis, and the torsion-free rank-one input, come from twisted-equivariant-equality. Uses cm-elliptic-reciprocity for (15.12.2).

items.name: Three characterizations of CM newforms
items.statement: Let f ∈ S_k(Γ1(N)) be a normalized newform with k≥2. The following are equivalent: (a) f has a nontrivial self-twist in the sense of ModularForms Layer 9, i.e. f = primitive(f⊗χ) with χ≠1; (b) f has CM in Kato's sense (Remark 12.8): there are an imaginary quadratic K and a continuous Hecke character ψ with L(f,s)=L(ψ,s); (c) f is the newform θ_ψ attached to an algebraic Hecke character ψ of an imaginary quadratic K of infinity type (1−k,0). In that case χ=ε_K; in (b), ψ may be replaced by ψ∘c so that it has type (1−k,0), and its conductor f_ψ satisfies N=|d_K|·N(f_ψ), with the nebentypus determined by ψ and ε_K.
items.locator: BT §2.2.5, p.5; Kato Remark 12.8 (p.223) and 15.10 (p.260); Ribet, LNM 601 (1977) (Kato's [Ri2])
items.note: Import the Layer 9 self-twist predicate; do not define a second one. BT's own proofs (Theorems 2.6, 3.1 and 1.1) need only the direction from ψ to f; this item is the interface with Kato §15, with Layer 9 and with Kato's non-CM case (12.8.1–12.8.2). It covers the algebraicity of ψ, its conductor and F⊂K(ψ(K^×)) through (b)⇔(c).

items.name: Kato's rational main conjecture for every CM newform and prime
items.statement: Let f∈S_k(Γ₁(N)) be a normalized CM newform of weight k≥2, p any prime, F its Hecke field and λ|p. With Kato's V,H^q and Z(f), ξ(H²_Iw(V))=ξ(H¹_Iw(V)/Z(f)) as ideals of Λ_Q=O_λ[[G_∞]][1/p].
items.note: No integral equality, p-adic L-function, residual irreducibility, good reduction or ordinary hypothesis is asserted. BT's proof overstates Kato: §15 gives only the inequality (Prop. 15.17). Equality needs equality-descent, with twisted-equivariant-equality on the ψ-components. Passing from H(T~) and Z(ψ,T) to H(V(f)) and Z(f) uses cm-galois-induction and cm-comparison-map; V_{Lλ}(ψ) is cm-realization.

items.name: Bloch–Kato finite local condition
items.statement: For a p-adic representation V of G_{Q_p}, H¹_f(Q_p,V)=ker(H¹(Q_p,V)→H¹(Q_p,V⊗B_cris)); at primes ℓ≠p use the unramified subgroup. For the de Rham modular representations in §3, the dual exponential is compared with this finite subgroup on its stated domain.

items.name: Global Bloch–Kato Selmer group
items.statement: For the modular representation W=V_{F_λ}(f)(k/2), with k≥2 even, H¹_f(Q,W) is the subgroup of H¹(Q,W) satisfying the finite local conditions at every place; use Kato's extension convention to identify the away-from-p conditions.

items.name: Even-weight CM newform rank-zero converse
items.statement: Let f be a normalized CM newform of even weight k≥2, p any prime and λ|p in its Hecke field. If H¹_f(Q,V_{F_λ}(f)(k/2))=0, then ord_{s=k/2}L(s,f)=0.
items.note: The half-weight Tate twist and arithmetic center k/2 are essential. L(s,f) is newform-l-function.

items.name: Kato’s global duality sequence
items.statement: Kato (14.9.3), with (14.9.4), for K = Q and an O_λ-lattice T whose V is de Rham at p, obtained from (14.9.1) and the Bloch–Kato [BK2 §3] local duality of H¹_f; exact for p ≠ 2 and exact up to ×2 for p = 2, so exact after ⊗Q.

items.name: Global Euler characteristic over Z[1/p]
items.statement: Kato (14.9.5): Σ(−1)^q rank H^q(Z[1/p],T) = −rank T⁻, for T⁻ the (−1)-eigenspace of complex conjugation.

items.name: Local Euler characteristic
items.statement: Kato (14.9.6): the local Euler–Poincaré formula for H^q(Q_p,V).

items.name: No invariants in modular representations
items.statement: H⁰(Q,V_{F_λ}(f)(r)) = 0; BT need only r = k/2 with k even, for both f and f*.
items.locator: The fact invoked in the proof of Kato Prop. 14.11(1) (which itself states finiteness of H⁰(Q,T⊗Q/Z))
items.note: Imports AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1/R19.3. For r = k/2 purity suffices: Frobenius eigenvalues on V(f)(k/2) have absolute value ℓ^{−1/2}.

items.name: Local cohomology of modular representations
items.statement: Kato Prop. 14.12, for 1 ≤ r ≤ k−1.
items.note: (3) comes from the H²_loc part of Kato Thm 12.5(3), which is the node KatoEulerSystems:L4/cohomological-divisibility-one-direction; (1) from (14.9.6) and (3); (2) from the [BK2 §3] sequence. A KatoEulerSystems L4 source addition, as for modular-h1-free.

items.name: Selmer vanishing forces finite-level H² vanishing
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 3.1 including H¹_f(Q,V(f)(k/2))=0, and for a stable lattice T⊂V(f), H²(Z[1/p],T(k/2))⊗Q=0.
items.note: Derive through global duality with the contragredient/conjugate modular representation and its H⁰/local terms. At p=2 Kato's integral exactness is only up to factors of 2; rationalization is mandatory. Kato's (14.9.3) is applied twice: first to the Tate-dual lattice T(k/2)^*(1), a lattice in V(f*)(k/2) by (14.10.1), whose Selmer term the hypothesis controls, giving H¹_f(Q,V(f*)(k/2))=0 with (14.9.5) and Prop. 14.12; then to T(k/2). BT compress this into one citation. Inputs: kato-duality-sequence, global-euler-characteristic, local-euler-characteristic, modular-h0-vanishing for f*, modular-local-cohomology and conjugate-dual.

items.name: Twist and specialize the correctly signed zeta element
items.statement: For k≥2 even put ±=(−1)^{k/2−1} and choose γ∈V(f) with nonzero ± component under complex conjugation. Let z be the image of z_γ(f) under H¹_Iw(V(f))≃H¹_Iw(V(f)(k/2))→H¹(Z[1/p],T(k/2))⊗Q, using the compatible roots to twist.
items.note: The twist isomorphism is semilinear for the corresponding automorphism of Λ, not Λ-linear for an unchanged action.

items.name: The global H¹ space is one dimensional
items.statement: Under Theorem 3.1's hypotheses and equation (3.1), dim_{F_λ}(H¹(Z[1/p],T(k/2))⊗Q)=1: H⁰(Z[1/p],V(f)(k/2)) = 0 by modular-h0-vanishing, and dim V^{c=−1} = 1 because det = κ^{1−k}ε^{−1} takes the value −1 at complex conjugation; then (14.9.5) (global-euler-characteristic) gives dim = 1.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.1 after (3.2), p.6; Kato (14.9.5)
items.note: Generic Euler characteristics remain owned by ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.3; this exact specialization is an application in the converse branch.

items.name: The half-weight specialization prime
items.statement: For k≥2 even, q=ker(Λ→O_λ), where the continuous O_λ-algebra map sends σ_c to c^{−k/2}; work at its extension to Λ_Q.

items.name: H² vanishes at the central specialization prime
items.statement: Under Theorem 3.1's Selmer-vanishing hypothesis, at the just-defined q one has H²_Iw(V)_q=0. Derive it from finite-level H² vanishing by the specialization sequence of iwasawa-specialization and localized Nakayama.
items.note: Finite-level vanishing does not imply this for an arbitrary inverse system; the specific control comparison is required.

items.name: Specialization of Iwasawa cohomology at a twist
items.statement: Let T ⊂ V_{F_λ}(f) be a G_Q-stable O_λ-lattice, j ∈ Z, and q_j = ker(Λ → O_λ, σ_c ↦ c^{−j}), extended to Λ_Q, where its localisation is a DVR. The twist-then-specialise map H¹_Iw(V) ≃ H¹_Iw(V(j)) → H¹(Z[1/p],T(j))⊗Q is Λ-linear for the action of Λ on the target through Λ/q_j, hence factors through H¹_Iw(V)_{q_j}/q_jH¹_Iw(V)_{q_j}. In Kato's j_* convention there is an exact sequence 0 → H¹_Iw(V)_{q_j}/q_j → H¹(Z[1/p],T(j))⊗Q → H²_Iw(V)_{q_j}[q_j] → 0, and an isomorphism H²_Iw(V)_{q_j}/q_j ≅ H²(Z[1/p],T(j))⊗Q.

items.name: Main-conjecture equality makes the specialized zeta class a basis
items.statement: Under Theorem 3.1's hypotheses, for γ with γ^±≠0 and the specialization above, z is an F_λ-basis of H¹(Z[1/p],T(k/2))⊗Q. Use H²_Iw(V)_q=0, the characteristic-ideal equality of Theorem 2.6, rank-one H¹ and the sign-compatible Kato map.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.1, p.6; comparison to Kato printed p.242
items.note: Uses the injectivity of H¹_q/qH¹_q → H¹(Z[1/p],T(k/2))⊗Q from iwasawa-specialization.

items.name: The specialized basis is outside the finite local condition
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses, loc_p(z)∉H¹_f(Q_p,V(f)(k/2)). Indeed z is nonzero and already satisfies the away-from-p finite conditions; if its p-localization were finite it would lie in the zero global Bloch–Kato Selmer group.

items.name: Frobenius weights of modular representations at p
items.statement: Kato (14.10.4)–(14.10.5) at every prime p, including p | N: the eigenvalues of crystalline Frobenius on D_pst of V_{F_λ}(f) (with its Weil–Deligne representation) have the weights given there, so D_crys(V(f*)(k/2))^{φ=1}=0.
items.locator: Kato (14.10.4)–(14.10.5); needed in the last paragraph of the proof of Theorem 3.1, p.6
items.note: Uses the Frobenius part of Saito's compatibility at p, not only the inertial type.

items.name: H¹_g = H¹_f at the centre
items.statement: For a normalized newform f of even weight k≥2, any prime p and λ|p, D_cris(V_{F_λ}(f*)(k/2))^{φ=1}=0; hence H¹_g(Q_p,V_{F_λ}(f)(k/2)) = H¹_f(Q_p,V_{F_λ}(f)(k/2)), and exp*: H¹(Q_p,V(f)(k/2))/H¹_f → S(f)⊗_F F_λ is injective.
items.locator: Last paragraph of the proof of Theorem 3.1, p.6 (unstated); Kato Lemma 14.18, p.247 (Fontaine–Laffaille case only); Bloch–Kato §3
items.note: Proof: ker exp* = H¹_g (Bloch–Kato Prop. 3.8); dim H¹_g − dim H¹_f = dim D_crys(V(f*)(k/2))^{φ=1} (Bloch–Kato Cor. 3.8.4 with Kato (14.10.1)); that dimension is 0 by kato-frobenius-weights applied to f*, the Weil–Deligne representation at p being pure of weight −1; the quotient is one-dimensional by Prop. 14.12. For CM f this also follows directly from ψ at every p (at additive reduction D_cris = 0). Consumers: central-nonvanishing and conditional-converse. Recorded as source issue E16 in the errata record.

items.name: Reciprocity converts nonfinite localization into L-value nonvanishing
items.statement: For a normalized weight-k≥2 newform with k even, correctly signed γ, and its specialized Kato class z, loc_p(z)∉H¹_f(Q_p,V(f)(k/2)) implies L(k/2,f)≠0, using Kato's explicit reciprocity law and the injectivity of exp* on H¹/H¹_f (central-hg-equals-hf), with its period and local-factor comparisons.
items.locator: Last paragraph of the proof of Theorem 3.1, p.6; Kato Theorem 12.5(1)
items.note: Keep the p-imprimitive versus full L-value comparison in the proof. This is the source's central-value implication, not a claim that exp* has kernel H_f for every de Rham representation without qualifications. Steps: (a) exp*(loc_p z) is given by critical-reciprocity (KatoEulerSystems L3) at χ=1, r=k/2; (b) ker exp* = H¹_g (PadicHodgeRegulators L1); (c) central-hg-equals-hf; (d) L^{p}(f*,k/2) ≠ 0 implies L(f,k/2) ≠ 0, because L^{p} = L·P_p(p^{−s}) and L(f*,s) = conj L(f,s̄) at real s. L(s,f) is newform-l-function.

items.name: Rational Kato main conjecture implies the even-weight rank-zero converse
items.statement: For any normalized elliptic newform f of even weight k≥2 and λ|p, assume Kato's rational cohomological main-conjecture equality in Theorem 2.6's conventions. Then H¹_f(Q,V(f)(k/2))=0 implies L(k/2,f)≠0.
items.note: Conditional in the non-CM case; it does not prove an unconditional rank-zero 2-converse for non-CM curves. L(s,f) is newform-l-function.

items.name: Hecke character of a CM elliptic curve
items.statement: For E/K with CM by an order of the imaginary quadratic field K, the Hecke character ψ_{E/K}: A_K^×/K^×→C^× of infinity type (−1,0), whose values on ideals prime to its conductor lie in K (as corrected in E15), and the comparison of V_pE⊗_{Q_p}L_λ with V_{L_λ}(ψ)⊕V_{L_λ}(ψ̄) as G_K-representations.
items.note: Used by cm-elliptic-factorization and cm-selmer-comparison.

items.name: CM elliptic L-function factors through two CM newforms
items.statement: For E/K as in Theorem 1.1, the associated Hecke character ψ and its conjugate determine weight-two CM newforms f and bar f, with Hecke fields contained in K, and L(s,E/K)=L(s,ψ)L(s,bar ψ)=L(s,f)L(s,bar f), with all local factors and arithmetic normalizations matched. Hence L(s,E/K) has an entire continuation and ord_{s=1}L(s,E/K)=ord_{s=1}L(s,f)+ord_{s=1}L(s,f̄).
items.note: CM.4 supplies the characters and Tate components; ER.5's maximal-order/class-number-one regulator example is not the full arbitrary-order and K-curve factorization. The Hecke character of E and the splitting of V_pE are cm-curve-hecke-character. L(s,f) is newform-l-function. L(s,ψ) is hecke-l-function. State it for Mathlib's W.LFunction, either as an equality of formal Dirichlet series (the Dirichlet convolution of the coefficient sequences of f and f̄) or for the L-series on the half-plane of absolute convergence, and then deduce the continuation. The local factors follow Mathlib's convention: minimal model, and factor 1 at primes of additive reduction, which are the primes where ψ ramifies.

items.name: CM Selmer vanishing compares with the two modular Selmer groups
items.statement: For E/K as in Theorem 1.1 and every prime p, corank_{Z_p}Sel_{p∞}(E/K)=0 implies H¹_f(Q,V_{F_λ}(f)(1))=0 and H¹_f(Q,V_{bar F_barλ}(bar f)(1))=0 after a common finite coefficient extension at p, for the associated weight-two CM forms. This is the vanishing consequence of the CM decomposition, induction/Shapiro, coefficient extension and the elliptic Kummer–Bloch–Kato comparison.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.1, p.6, Selmer comparison display
items.note: The author PDF writes a schematic isomorphism involving the Pontryagin dual, ⊗K, and untwisted V. Do not copy it as a typed literal isomorphism: Kato (8.3),(14.10.2) and Theorem 3.1 require the weight-two twist (1), completed coefficients, and a duality dictionary. This item deliberately states only the vanishing implication actually used. The design must prove the typed comparison, not assume the printed shorthand. Uses cm-curve-hecke-character and the k=2 case of cm-galois-induction (coordinated with PAPER-DOSPINESCU-LEBRAS-17/hecke-cm-forms).

items.name: Selmer coranks over a quadratic field
items.statement: For E/Q, a quadratic field K and any prime p, corank_{Z_p}Sel_{p∞}(E/K)=corank_{Z_p}Sel_{p∞}(E/Q)+corank_{Z_p}Sel_{p∞}(E^K/Q). The comparison uses restriction/corestriction and the ± eigenspaces of Gal(K/Q); it is an isomorphism for odd p, and for p=2 its kernels and cokernels are finite 2-primary groups.
items.locator: Implicit in the proof of Theorem 1.1, p.6 (input to cm-corank-double)
items.note: BSD.1 plans the finite-level/primary-part comparison and the rank identity; pass to p∞ coranks with selmer-exact and the corank carrier.

items.name: Selmer corank doubles under CM base change
items.statement: If E/Q has CM by an order in an imaginary quadratic K and p is any prime, then corank_{Z_p}Sel_{p∞}(E/K)=2·corank_{Z_p}Sel_{p∞}(E/Q). Moreover corank_{Z_p}Sel_{p∞}(E/Q) = corank_{Z_p}Sel_{p∞}(E^K/Q) for every p: the self-twist isogeny φ and its dual induce maps on Sel_{p∞} with φ̂∘φ = [deg φ], hence finite kernel and cokernel.
items.locator: Last paragraph of proof of Theorem 1.1, p.6
items.note: Use rational quadratic descent and the CM self-twist isogeny. At p=2 retain finite restriction/corestriction errors; no integral direct-sum statement follows. The corank comes from SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2 and the finite-level φ-Kummer maps from EllipticCurves Layer 7. Uses quadratic-selmer-descent with cm-self-twist.

items.name: L-function of E over a quadratic field
items.statement: For E/Q and a quadratic field K with quadratic twist E^K, L(s,E/K)=L(s,E/Q)·L(s,E^K/Q) as actual analytic L-functions, with every local factor matched including bad primes. Hence ord_{s=1}L(s,E/K)=ord_{s=1}L(s,E/Q)+ord_{s=1}L(s,E^K/Q).
items.locator: Implicit in the proof of Theorem 1.1, p.6 (input to cm-order-double)

items.name: Analytic order doubles under CM base change
items.statement: If E/Q has CM by an order in an imaginary quadratic K, ord_{s=1}L(s,E/K)=2·ord_{s=1}L(s,E/Q).
items.locator: Last paragraph of proof of Theorem 1.1, p.6
items.note: Use BSD.0's factorization and the CM self-twist isogeny; prove the local-factor comparison rather than equating analytic germs by definition. Uses quadratic-l-factorization with cm-self-twist.

items.name: 2∞-Selmer parity for congruent-number twists
items.statement: For positive squarefree n, (−1)^{corank_{Z_2}Sel_{2∞}(E^(n)/Q)} = w(E^(n)/Q) for E:y²=x³−x. With congruent-root-number, corank_{Z_2}Sel_{2∞}(E^(n)/Q) is even for n≡1,2,3 mod 8.
items.locator: Used implicitly in deriving Theorem 3.3, p.6, from Smith [21, Thm. 1.2]; root numbers from footnote 2, p.2
items.note: Source: Monsky, Generalizing the Birch–Stephens theorem I, Math. Z. 221 (1996), 415–420 (a prerequisite of PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22); its p=2 scope was not read here and must be confirmed at the source. For this family alone: compute the 2-Selmer rank parity of E^(n) (Monsky's appendix to Heath-Brown), then use the alternating Cassels–Tate pairing to get r_2 ≡ r_{2∞} mod 2. Do not identify finite 2-Selmer rank with 2∞-corank.

items.name: Smith's 2∞-Selmer density input
items.statement: For E:y²=x³−x, a relative-density-one subset of positive squarefree n≡1,2,3 (mod 8) has corank_{Z_2}Sel_{2∞}(E^(n)/Q)=0.
items.note: Smith's displayed Theorem 1.2 counts all nonzero signed integers and assumes his Assumption 1.1; for this curve use the full rational 2-torsion/no rational cyclic 4-isogeny case, 2-parity (congruent-2-parity with congruent-root-number), and the squarefree/local-family comparison to obtain BT's restricted density. Do not identify finite 2-Selmer rank with 2∞-corank.

items.name: BKLOS 3∞-Selmer density input for CM twists
items.statement: For K imaginary quadratic, E/K with CM by an order in K, and 3 not inert in K, the lower limiting proportion of t∈K×/(K×)², ordered by H(t), with corank_{Z_3}Sel_{3∞}(E^(t)/K)=0 is at least 1/2.
items.note: BKLOS Theorem 2.7's headline is Mordell–Weil rank. Its proof gives the needed stronger Selmer assertion: maximal-order 3-isogeny with global Selmer ratio 1, average 3-Selmer rank ≤1 and even parity ⇒ at least half have zero 3-Selmer rank; transfer rational corank along an isogeny for a nonmaximal order. No finite-Sha assumption is inserted. Finite torsion-exception squareclasses have density zero and must be removed before using the torsion-free rank count.

items.name: Cube-sum curves satisfy the CM-twist hypotheses
items.statement: For every n∈Z\{0}, the smooth projective cubic E_n:x³+y³=2n with its rational point at infinity is an elliptic curve; over K=Q(ζ₃) it has CM by an order of K and 3 is ramified, so Proposition 1.3 applies to its quadratic twists over K.
items.note: This is not a positive-density theorem for rational cube sums as n varies.

items.name: Descending twists are thin
items.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic and E/K have CM by an order of K. Then j(E) ∈ Q, and the set of t ∈ K^×/(K^×)² with E^(t) ≅ E'_K for some E'/Q lies in at most two cosets of the image of Q^×/(Q^×)² (one when j(E) ≠ 1728). Each such coset has O(X^{1/2}) classes with H(t)<X, while all of K^×/(K^×)² has ≍X. Hence the set has H-density zero.
items.note: Twist classification by K^×/K^×² for j≠0,1728, by sextic and quartic twists for j=0,1728 (work modulo 4th powers at j=1728); H as in number-field-twist-height; bounded-height finiteness from ST.0.

items.name: Positive proportion of analytic-rank-zero twists not descending to Q
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 1.3 (K imaginary quadratic, E/K with CM by an order of K, 3 not inert in K), the set of t ∈ K^×/(K^×)² with ord_{s=1}L(s,E^(t)/K)=0 and E^(t) not isomorphic to a base change E'_K of any E'/Q has lower H-density at least 1/2; in particular it is positive, as in Remark 3.6(ii).
items.note: Keep as a separately proved counting/descent consequence. The source's historical 'first examples' qualification is not mathematical content. From cm-twist-density and twist-descent-thin by inclusion–exclusion.

items.name: Complex-conjugation sign of the Kato map
items.statement: For f,p,λ as in Theorem 2.4 and ι the complex-conjugation action on V(f), z_{ι(γ)}(f)=−σ_{−1}z_γ(f). Consequently the q-specialization at σ_c↦c^{−k/2} selects the sign (−1)^{k/2−1} when k is even.
items.locator: Choice of γ in proof of Theorem 3.1, p.6; Kato Theorem 12.5(1), printed p.221
items.note: The sign relation is needed to pass from the module generated by all γ to the selected nonzero sign component; it is not a choice of an arbitrary generator. For CM f this follows from cm-h2-torsion by Kato 13.8 and 13.9–13.13 (Kato 15.16); (15.16.1) itself uses 12.4(2). Kato states 15.16 only for K ⊄ Q(μ_{p∞}); for K ⊂ Q(μ_{p∞}) (K=Q(i), p=2) the same deduction applies, since 13.9–13.13 use only 12.4 and 13.5–13.6.

items.name: Duality convention for the conjugate modular form
items.statement: For Kato's weight-k representation, V_{F_λ}(f*)≃Hom_{F_λ}(V_{F_λ}(f),F_λ)(1−k), over the same F_λ (F is stable under complex conjugation, Kato 6.3). Thus the Tate dual of V(f)(r) is the representation of f* twisted by k−r.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.1 via Kato (14.9.3); Kato (14.10.1), printed p.240
items.note: This comparison is required in the duality argument; it is not the assertion that every nebentypus representation is self-dual.

items.name: Classical p∞-Selmer and Bloch–Kato vanishing comparison
items.statement: For E over a number field F and any prime p, the classical Kummer local conditions on V_pE identify the rational classical Selmer space with H¹_f(F,V_pE). In particular corank_{Z_p}Sel_{p∞}(E/F)=0 if and only if H¹_f(F,V_pE)=0. Compare dual vector spaces when using the Pontryagin dual; no canonical identification of a vector space with its dual is assumed.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.1, p.6, comparison display; Kato §14.9 conventions
items.note: Route the general Kummer/Bloch–Kato comparison to the existing Selmer owner; the CM decomposition itself is a separate item.

items.name: A rational CM elliptic curve is isogenous to its CM quadratic twist
items.statement: If E/Q has CM by an order O of an imaginary quadratic field K, then E is Q-isogenous to its quadratic twist E^K = E.quadraticTwist K (EllipticCurves Layer 5, `WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwist`). The isogeny is ι∘α, where α ∈ O has ᾱ = −α and ι : E_K ≅ E^K_K is the twist isomorphism. It induces a Q_p[G_Q]-isomorphism V_p(E) ≅ V_p(E^K) for every p, including p dividing deg α (R01.6 isogeny compatibility).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.1, final paragraph, p.6 (input to the doubling identities)
items.note: This concrete CM application imports ideal actions/isogenies and quadratic descent; it does not replace an isogeny by a Q-isomorphism.

items.name: CM newforms are induced from Hecke characters
items.statement: For a newform f of weight k≥2 and level N with L(f,s)=L(ψ,s), ψ of type (1−k,0) and conductor dividing N: F⊂L, and V_{Lλ}(f)≅Ind_{G_K}^{G_Q}V_{Lλ}(ψ) as G_Q-representations over L_λ, in Kato's cohomological normalization with his explicit action in 15.10; the induced representation is irreducible. After fixing (15.11.1) S(ψ)≅S(f)⊗_F L, there is a unique Galois isomorphism (15.11.2) compatible with (15.8.1) and D_dR, and a unique Gal(C/R)-isomorphism (15.11.3) compatible with per_ψ and per_f.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.6, p.5; Kato 15.10 p.260 and Lemma 15.11 pp.260–262
items.note: Proof inputs: Frobenius characteristic polynomials at primes ∤Np from cm-l-function and R19.1's Eichler–Shimura relation, Chebotarev with Brauer–Nesbitt, and irreducibility of V(f) (Kato's [Ri2], Ribet LNM 601). Its weight-2 case coincides with PAPER-DOSPINESCU-LEBRAS-17/hecke-cm-forms: one owner states it (CM.4 through this route) and the other imports it; coordinate also with the CM-form items PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-23 routes to R19.2. Routed once, as a source item for ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.4, which already requires AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.3 and which both Part II designs import.

items.name: The three even-parity residue classes occupy half the squarefree family
items.statement: Among positive squarefree integers ordered by n≤X, the limiting proportion with n≡1,2,3 (mod 8) is 1/2. A relative-density-one subset of these classes consequently has density 1/2 in the full positive squarefree family.
items.locator: Theorem 1.2, p.2 and its abstract formulation; counting comparison used in §3.2.1
items.note: Requires squarefree residue-class asymptotics; do not count all eight residue classes with equal weights.

prerequisites.citation: Johnson-Leung–Kings, On the equivariant main conjecture for imaginary quadratic fields, J. Reine Angew. Math. 653 (2011), 75–114.
prerequisites.why: BT Theorem 2.1 needs its regular height-one argument (§7.2) and character/determinant comparison. No existing roadmap has this source-specific imaginary-quadratic elliptic-unit proof; the rational branch must not inherit an unnecessary μ=0 condition.

routes.reason: Use BT Theorems 2.3–2.4 and Remark 2.5 to require the exact all-prime rational Kato inputs: H² torsion, H¹ rank-one freeness, the zeta map, its sign relation and critical-value reciprocity. Read Kato §§12–15 for the actual proofs. L2 owns the constructed classes and signs, L3 the regulator/period/local-factor formula (with f*, not f, in Kato's display), and L4 the nonvanishing/cohomological theorems. This does not put the reverse CM divisibility in the one-divisibility layer. L4's Euler-system bound (Kato Thm 13.4) does not apply to CM f, whose H² torsion and H¹ freeness come from the elliptic-unit layer of route 7 (item cm-h2-torsion); the L4 inputs here are for non-CM f or conditional on Kato 12.4(2).

The source fixes Kato's j_* étale extension (identified with unramified local conditions by the new item jstar-selmer-comparison, which SelmerIwasawaCohomology does not yet own), lattice/rational coefficients, strict and Bloch–Kato conditions, Kummer comparisons and specialization maps. Add the precise elliptic Kummer–Bloch–Kato vanishing comparison to L4, including duals; import finite-level Selmer/Sha from EllipticCurves Layer 7 and local finite conditions from PadicHodgeRegulators L1. Generic compact cochain duality stays with ArithmeticGaloisDuality, arithmetic unit/class inverse limits with IntegralIwasawaTheory I.2. It also receives congruent-2-parity (2∞-Selmer parity for the congruent-number twists), next to Nekovář's Selmer parity (PAPER-SKINNER-20/18), which was accepted at L4.

ST.5 receives BKLOS's 3∞ corank consequence, whose prerequisite paper must be decomposed there (Smith's 2∞ result goes to the Smith-method Part II, route 9); Bhargava–Shankar's average over all curves is not a proof for a thin quadratic-twist family. Keep the BKLOS isogeny/rational-corank step explicit. Analytic-rank conclusions are consumers of these theorems, not alternate definitions of them. bklos-density imports its complex-multiplication inputs rather than re-planning them in ST.5. From ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.1 it takes the order and ideal action; the ideal-kernel 3-isogeny E→E/E[𝔭] for 𝔭 of norm 3, with End ≅ O_K; the normalized action of O_K on the invariant differential (used for α_{a,𝔭}=|a|_𝔭^{-1}); and the K-isogeny from a curve with CM by an order to one with CM by O_K (BKLOS §11; Rubin, Prop. 5.3). No cycle arises: ST.5 has no consumers, and the closure of CM.1 contains no ArithmeticStatistics stage.

Reuse the arithmetic tower and norm-compatible inverse-limit carriers. BT supplies the CM two-variable example and distinguishes the full cyclotomic group from its Z_p quotient. The particular ray-tower group/rank and elliptic-unit equalities remain new CM-branch statements, not claims that the cyclotomic/totally-real main conjectures already prove them.

This concrete root-number computation fits BSD.0's root-number parity and quadratic-twist local factors, which RS-30 keeps.
