routes.brief:
Design "Main conjectures for modular forms and their families, Part II: all-prime CM zeta-element main conjectures", with ModularIwasawaMainConjectures as its first prerequisite. The final theorem is BT Theorem 2.6: for every normalized CM newform f of weight k≥2, every rational prime p and every place λ|p of its Hecke field, char(H²_Iw(V(f)))=char(H¹_Iw(V(f))/Z(f)) over O_λ[[Gal(Q(μ_{p∞})/Q)]][1/p], in Kato's cohomological representation and étale extension conventions. Prove, as its arithmetic input, BT Theorem 2.1 in corrected form: for every imaginary quadratic K, nonzero ideal f and prime p, char((h¹/z)[1/p])=char(h²[1/p])·∏_{𝔩|f,𝔩∤p}char(Z_p[[G/D_𝔩]][1/p]) over Z_p[[Gal(K(p∞f)/K)]][1/p], equivalently with h² replaced by the Iwasawa H² over O_K[1/pf] as in Johnson-Leung–Kings. As printed, BT omit these Euler factors (z uses only the modulus-p^n f elliptic units); the printed form holds on the ψ-components used for Theorem 2.6, where every such 𝔩 is ramified. These are rational, not integral, equalities.

Import the parent L0's formulation; Arithmetic Iwasawa theory and the main conjecture (IntegralIwasawaTheory I.1–I.2) for arithmetic towers and norm-compatible unit/class modules; Dirichlet p-adic L-functions, special values, and Eisenstein measures, Part II: Ray-class and automorphic interpolation (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0) for the ray-class inverse limit and its dimension formula; Global number fields (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields Layer 2) for ray class carriers; Kato classes and explicit reciprocity for modular forms (KatoEulerSystems L0) for Siegel functions and their distribution relations; Complex multiplication and explicit reciprocity (ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.1–CM.4) for CM pairs, ideal actions and characters; Class field theory (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory Layer 13) for actual ray class fields; Profinite and pro-p groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 9 prerequisites) for the completed Z_p group algebra Z_p[[G_{p^∞f}]]; Profinite and pro-p groups, Part II: p-adic measures and Iwasawa algebras (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1/L4/L5) for general coefficients, height-one divisors and specialization with Tor; Selmer groups, continuous integral cohomology, and Iwasawa cohomology (SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0/L3/L4) for Kummer/cohomological comparisons; Continuous cohomology of profinite groups, Part II: compact coefficients and arithmetic duality (ArithmeticGaloisDuality) for the common cochains and duality; and Kato classes and explicit reciprocity for modular forms (KatoEulerSystems L2–L4) for constructed Beilinson–Kato elements, signs, rational H¹ freeness and H² torsion for non-CM f, and the modular-curve reciprocity law only. Kato's elliptic-unit reciprocity (Prop. 15.9 and (15.12.2), item cm-elliptic-reciprocity) is proved here.

Import the CM ray tower and G≃Z_p²×Δ_f (without assuming p∤#Δ_f) from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0, and verify finite generation, torsion-freeness/generic rank of h¹, torsion of h² and h¹/z. Construct actual elliptic units with their admissibility, smoothing, norm and auxiliary-independence laws. Prove the Kummer and class/H² comparisons, retaining the p-place/Brauer pseudo-null corrections. Prove the localization sequence 0→H²(O[1/p])→H²(O[1/pf])→⊕_{𝔩|f,𝔩∤p}Z_p[[G/D_𝔩]]→0 of Iwasawa cohomology and the vanishing of its last term on components ramified at 𝔩; it links JLK's formulation to BT's class-group h². Decompose Johnson-Leung–Kings §7.2's regular-prime proof and its Rubin/Huber–Kings inputs. Exclude the singular-prime μ condition from the rational target only because p has been inverted; do not assert the integral non-split case.

Prove Kato's actual elliptic-unit/Beilinson–Kato identity (15.16.1), with the normalized fraction-field elliptic-unit element and its height-one span. Construct Kato's realization V_{Lλ}(ψ) with S(ψ), per_ψ and (15.8.1) (item cm-realization) and the comparison map (15.12.1) (item cm-comparison-map), import the induction isomorphism V(f)≅Ind V(ψ) with (15.11.2)–(15.11.3) from CM.4 (item cm-galois-induction), and carry out twisting and one-variable descent through (15.13.1)–(15.13.2) and coefficient descent. Kato §15 proves only the inequality (Prop. 15.17), so BT's "it is shown in [12, §15]" overstates it: prove the equality step separately. Apply Kato's Lemma 14.15 to both H²_q and H¹_q/A·z; the Ker(a|H²) terms of (15.13.1)–(15.13.2) cancel, and Ker(a|H¹_q/Az)=0 because A is regular local, a is prime, H¹_q is torsion-free of rank one and z generates it at aA (Kato 15.15). Treat K⊂Q(μ_{p∞}) separately via §15.14; K=Q(i), p=2 is an acceptance test, not an excluded corner case. Do not infer specialization from equality of divisors alone.

Every definition needs a use-derived API and at least three mathematical tests in the subsequent blueprint: norm compatibility, auxiliary-ideal independence, coefficient extension, bad-prime factors and the dyadic finite factor. Export named rational equalities and the precise normalization dictionary to CMRankZeroConverse. No ordinary p-adic L-function, integral BSD formula, or extra prime restriction is a substitute for the stated endpoints.

Coordinate with the designs of InertAnticyclotomicCMMainConjecture (issue #1690, also a Part II of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures) and NonordinaryCMSpecialValues (issue #1689), which need the same Kato §15.5 elliptic-unit tower and the general Prop. 15.9 (item cm-elliptic-reciprocity) in that shared early layer; PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21/elliptic-reciprocity is its r=1 specialization and imports it rather than proving 15.9 again. Put the elliptic-unit and tower-module foundations in an early layer that does not depend on the rational main conjecture, owned here and imported by the others. Keep the early elliptic-unit and tower-module layer, which depends on no main conjecture and is owned here; its consumers are the BKO designs (#1689, #1690) and HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.7s, which needs Rubin 1987's elliptic-unit route. Then add an integral layer, owned here. It proves Johnson-Leung–Kings Theorem 5.2 as printed (Div κ_χ = 0 over Λ_O = O[[Gal(K_∞/K)]], for every character χ and every p), and JLK §5.4's classical form char(p_{χ⁻¹}E_∞/I_ΛJ_Λ(ζ(χ))) = char(p_{χ⁻¹}A_∞) for p ∤ #Δ, which is Rubin 1991 (i), with Rubin's exact hypotheses checked against Rubin 1991. For p split, the same layer proves the Coleman-map/Katz form, Rubin 1991 (ii), including the anticyclotomic θ-components, the λ-equality and the functional equation of PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22 route 8 (its item 9); it imports Katz's measure from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3, and the two-variable Coleman map is new here. The integral equivariant Ω-form stays excluded (JLK §7.3, μ = 0). The rational equivariant layers (items equivariant-main and regular-prime-equality) then follow. Consumers of the integral layer: InertAnticyclotomicCMMainConjecture (PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21/rubin-two-variable-input) and RankZeroOneBSD BSD.7a (PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22 item 9). Neither the elliptic-unit layer nor the integral layer may depend, directly or transitively, on ModularIwasawaMainConjectures L6 or RankZeroOneBSD BSD.7a, since BSD.7a feeds MIMC L6; importing MIMC L0 is allowed.

Prove the CM case of Kato 12.4 (item cm-h2-torsion) in the elliptic-unit layer, before any Kato class is used, from Rubin's theorem (Kato 15.2), (15.12.2) and (15.13.1), with the §15.14 form for K ⊂ Q(μ_{p∞}). Import from KatoEulerSystems L2–L4 only statements that are conditional on 12.4(2) or restricted to non-CM f.

routes.title: Rank-zero and rank-one Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer theory, Part II: CM rank-zero converses and twist nonvanishing
routes.reason: The parent proves the analytic-to-arithmetic implication and selected leading-term formulas, not the Selmer-to-analytic converse. RankOneConverse, the other Part II of RankZeroOneBSD (DESIGN-SKINNER #951, with routes from PAPER-SKINNER-20 and PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22), owns the non-CM converses in analytic ranks 0 and 1: Skinner's Theorems A, A′, C and E, and CGLS Theorem 5.2.1 (r ∈ {0,1}, Eisenstein primes of good reduction). Those proofs go through Heegner points over an auxiliary K and use only the forward Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin/Kato direction. This route proves the CM rank-zero converse through the all-prime CM zeta-element main conjecture and Kato's reciprocity law. The hypotheses are disjoint and neither roadmap supplies or consumes the other.
routes.brief:
Design "Rank-zero and rank-one Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer theory, Part II: CM rank-zero converses and twist nonvanishing", with RankZeroOneBSD as its first prerequisite. Prove BT Theorem 3.1: for a normalized CM newform f of even weight k≥2, any p and λ|p, H¹_f(Q,V_{F_λ}(f)(k/2))=0 implies L(k/2,f)≠0. Then prove Theorem 1.1: for E/K with K imaginary quadratic and CM by any order of K, and any prime p, corank_{Z_p}Sel_{p∞}(E/K)=0 implies L(1,E/K)≠0; include the descended E/Q conclusion for every p. State Remark 3.2 as a conditional theorem for non-CM even-weight newforms assuming the rational Kato equality, not an unconditional non-CM converse.

Import Elliptic curves, Part II: rank-zero and rank-one Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer theory (RankZeroOneBSD BSD.0–BSD.1) for actual analytic L-functions, twists and quadratic descent; Modular forms (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms Layer 7) for the analytic rank of the newform L-functions; Elliptic curves (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves Layer 7) for finite-level and isogeny Selmer groups and Kummer sequences; the design proves the invariance of Sel_{p∞} coranks under isogeny; the separately designed all-prime CM zeta-element branch (CMAllPrimeMainConjectures) for Theorem 2.6; Kato classes and explicit reciprocity for modular forms (KatoEulerSystems L2–L4) for the actual class, sign relation and regulator formula; Selmer groups, continuous integral cohomology, and Iwasawa cohomology (SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2–L4) and P-adic regulators and the local K₃ calculation (PadicHodgeRegulators L1) for finite local conditions, ker exp* = H¹_g and the H¹_g/H¹_f dimension formula; Continuous cohomology of profinite groups, Part II: compact coefficients and arithmetic duality (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3/R02.4/D7) for Euler characteristics and rational Poitou–Tate; Galois representations attached to modular and Hilbert modular forms (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1/R19.3/R19.5) for Kato's realization and conjugate-dual comparison; Complex multiplication and explicit reciprocity (ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.1/CM.4) for CM character factorization and the self-twist isogeny.

Split the proof into named statements: Selmer zero gives finite-level H² zero; Euler–Poincaré gives H¹ dimension one; define q by σ_c↦c^{−k/2}; prove the control/Tor comparison and localized H² vanishing; the main conjecture and γ^{(−1)^{k/2−1}}≠0 yield a specialized zeta basis; this class fails the finite condition at p; H¹_g = H¹_f at the centre, so exp* is injective on H¹/H¹_f (Saito's crystalline Frobenius polynomial and weights, Kato (14.10.4)–(14.10.5); items central-hg-equals-hf, kato-frobenius-weights); reciprocity gives nonzero central L-value. Match Kato's f* and p-omitted L-value with f and the full arithmetic L-function. At p=2 retain real-place integral errors before rationalization.

For the elliptic specialization, prove a typed Kummer/Bloch–Kato, CM decomposition and induction/Shapiro comparison with completed coefficients. The author version's p.6 display suppresses duals and the weight-two Tate twist: it must not become an unchecked literal isomorphism. The supplied extraction records only the required vanishing implication. Prove both doubling identities for descent to Q using the self-twist isogeny and rational ± decomposition, not an integral direct sum at p=2.

Finally import Arithmetic statistics, counting fields and Selmer distributions (ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.5), with the two source routes in this extraction. Combine Smith's relative-density-one corank-zero statement with p=2 to obtain BT Theorem 1.2 for E:y²=x³−x and positive squarefree n≡1,2,3 mod 8; establish density 1/2 among all positive squarefree n, without asserting the odd-parity analytic-rank-one half. Combine BKLOS's corank-zero input with p=3 to obtain Proposition 1.3 for CM E/K with 3 split or ramified, in the exact squareclass height H(t)=∏_{v_𝔭(t) odd}N𝔭, as a lower proportion at least 1/2. Include the cube-sum family E_n:x³+y³=2n over Q(ζ₃) and the positive-proportion non-descent consequence in Remark 3.6, whose counting input is twist-descent-thin (descending twists have H-density zero).

Require use-derived APIs and at least three tests per new definition: p=2 and K=Q(i), ramified 3, nonmaximal CM orders, the correct half-weight/sign, wrong-parity vectors, lower versus exact density, and finite 2-Selmer rank versus 2∞-corank. No integral BSD valuation, unrestricted rank-r converse or positive-proportion cube-sum theorem is claimed.

The p-converse to Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin (DESIGN-SKINNER, issue #951, RankOneConverse), which also owns rank-zero converses for non-CM curves (Skinner's Theorem E; CGLS Theorem 5.2.1 with r = 0), is also a Part II of RankZeroOneBSD. The rank-r p-converse proposition (item p-converse-property) should have one owner: whichever design is written first defines it and the other imports it. converse-q and CGLS Theorem 5.2.1 are stated as instances of p-converse-property. Skinner's Theorem E (hypothesis A_f(Q), Ш(A_f) finite) and converse-k/newform-converse are not instances.

Import the k=2 case of cm-galois-induction from ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.4 (coordinated with PAPER-DOSPINESCU-LEBRAS-17/hecke-cm-forms) and the Hecke character of E (cm-curve-hecke-character) for the Selmer comparison.

State also modular-h0-vanishing (H⁰(Q,V(f)(r)) = 0) and import modular-local-cohomology (Kato Prop. 14.12) for the Selmer-to-H² step.

The control comparison at q is imported from SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3 (item iwasawa-specialization) and applied at q, not proved again.

Also state the even parity Goldfeld conjecture of §1.0.2 (fundamental discriminants of both signs, ordered by |d|) and prove it for y²=x³−x from Theorem 1.2 by the comparison in goldfeld-fundamental.

Import Theorem 3.3 from ArithmeticStatisticsPartIISmithMethod (route 9) and BKLOS's corank input from ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.5.
